why_how.text: Ohio prohibits operating or knowingly allowing a vehicle on a highway when its unsafe condition endangers anyone.
A vehicle must not carry protruding objects, sharp broken edges or parts that could injure someone touching them.
The steering mechanism should work normally without excessive looseness at the steering wheel.
Vehicle tires need at least one sixteenth of an inch of tread and must have no major bulges, bumps or damage.
An average motor vehicle should have at least two safety belts in its front seat.
The service brake must provide enough braking to slow, stop and control the vehicle.
The parking brake must be capable of keeping the vehicle stationary on a slope.
A vehicle should have two functioning headlights, with one mounted on each side.
The vehicle should have two red rear reflectors that can be seen from three hundred feet.
At least one red taillight should be visible from five hundred feet.
The vehicle should have two red brake lights visible from five hundred feet when braking.
A white lamp should make the rear license plate visible from fifty feet.
Working turn signals should include two front signals and two rear signals, visible from three hundred feet.
Windshield wipers must function well enough to remove precipitation from the windshield.
The rear-view mirror should give the driver a clear, unobstructed view behind the vehicle.
A functioning vehicle horn should be recognizable as a motor vehicle horn and audible from two hundred feet.
The exhaust system should remain in good working condition and operate continuously.
The windshield light-transmission standard stated in the handbook is seventy percent.
The handbook allows fifty percent light transmission through front-seat side windows, with a tolerance of three percentage points in either direction.
Use the vehicle identification number to search the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration website for safety recalls.

why_how.text: Too little air, too much air or insufficient tread in a tire can create road-safety problems.
Use the vehicle maker's recommended tire pressure shown on the door jamb.
Measure tire pressure when the tires have reached the temperature of the surrounding air.
To measure tire pressure, take off the valve-stem cap and apply a pressure gauge.
Add air when tire pressure is below the recommended level, or let air out through the valve when pressure is above it.
For a penny tread check, put Lincoln's head into the deepest tire groove; seeing his entire head means the tire is too worn to drive on and needs replacement.
Ohio permits studded tires from November first through April fifteenth.
Use headlights between sunset and sunrise, when visibility is poor, and whenever precipitation requires windshield-wiper use.
High beams may be used while headlights are needed, except when a vehicle is approaching from the opposite direction.
Use turn signals to announce a turn, a change in direction or a lane change on a road with multiple lanes.
Start the turn signal at least one hundred feet before changing direction.
Hazard lights help others see a vehicle that has stopped on the roadway or nearby.

why_how.text: Sit upright with your back supported by the seat and your feet on the floor.
Before moving, position the seat for a clear windshield view, full pedal and steering control, and enough room for air-bag deployment.
A properly positioned seat lets your foot pivot easily between brake and accelerator while your heel stays on the floor.
With the seat correctly adjusted, the steering-wheel top is no higher than your shoulders and remains below your chin.
Keep at least ten inches between your chest and the steering wheel to provide space for air-bag deployment.
Position the head restraint against the back of your head, at least as high as your ears, to help prevent whiplash.
Set the mirrors before driving so they provide the best available view beside and behind the vehicle.
Aim the interior rear-view mirror to frame the rear window and show traffic behind you.
For the left outside mirror, rest your head against the closed driver-side window and adjust until only a small part of the vehicle's left edge remains visible.
For the right outside mirror, lean until your head is over the center console, then adjust until the rear edge of your vehicle is barely visible.
The described outside-mirror adjustment adds twelve to sixteen degrees of view on each side, although the vehicle's sides are no longer visible in a normal mirror glance.
With the described mirror adjustment, a vehicle behind moves from the inside mirror to an outside mirror, then into the driver's peripheral view.

why_how.text: Air bags supplement safety belts and work best together with them to reduce the chance of the head or upper body striking the interior in a crash.
Consult the vehicle owner's manual for information specific to its air bags.
Drivers and front-seat riders in most passenger vehicles must wear safety belts on Ohio roads, including vehicles equipped with air bags.
Fasten your own safety belt and check that every passenger uses a safety belt or a child restraint.
For a driver younger than eighteen, occupancy cannot exceed the number of originally installed safety belts, and every occupant must wear one.
Place the safety belt over the body's bony shoulder and hip areas.
Wear the shoulder belt over the shoulder and chest with little or no slack, never under an arm or behind the back.
Incorrect shoulder-belt use can cause serious internal injury during a crash.
After fastening, tighten the lap belt so it sits low and snug across the hips.
A poorly positioned lap belt can let you slide out during a crash, causing injury or death.
